reasons: Claimed status is supported: the supplied paragraphs (5.2 editorial control, General Manager, 7.1 e-mail list cross-promotion, 8.1 confidentiality) contain no ownership or assignment language, so a 'missing' IP finding is appropriate for an agreement under which HDI develops and hosts the Site and handles Company Content and user data.

The inserted Section 5.5 hits every element of the preferred position: Company ownership of Content, Marks and deliverables with an express assignment by HDI; HDI retention of pre-existing platform/tools coupled with a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, sublicensable licence back for embedded HDI IP; exclusive Company ownership of Site customer/order data with a return obligation; and an express no-joint-ownership statement.

Edit is additive only — existing text (including p0035) is left intact — which is the smallest edit capable of curing silence, and the new clause is numbered/anchored consistently within Section 5 immediately after the last Section 5 paragraph supplied.

Comment is accurate, in the required voice and prefix, explains the addition, cites the playbook rationale, and correctly offers the licence-back fallback while holding the line on Content and customer data ownership; deterministic checks confirm no assignment of Customer IP/data to HDI was introduced.

Minor, non-fatal note for the drafter: sub-clause (c) limits HDI's use of Site customer e-mail lists to performance of its obligations, which sits slightly awkwardly with the reciprocal cross-promotion right in Section 7.1; a carve-out ('except as permitted under Section 7.1') would avoid an internal conflict, though the current wording errs in our favour.
